The test image shows a tomato stem with a distinct elongated brown/reddish canker running along the internode. The lesion is sunken and discolored brown-to-dark-reddish-brown, while the surrounding stem remains green. This is a classic stem canker presentation.

Key features:
- Affected part: stem (internode)
- Color: brown to reddish-brown longitudinal lesion
- Pattern: elongated streak/canker along stem
- No white mycelium, no leaf spots visible

Top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (brown stem streaking/canker) or Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.

Let me view a reference for Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato:

The reference for Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato shows an uprooted wilting plant with brown stem lesions — consistent with the disease pattern. The test image shows a close-up of a single internode with a longitudinal brown canker/streak that appears slightly cracked/sunken, which is characteristic of Bacterial Canker (caused by *Clavibacter michiganensis*). The vascular tissue within the stem shows the brown discoloration typical of this disease.

The Bugwood ID 1573600 in the test image also corresponds to known bacterial canker images. The elongated, well-defined stem canker with brown interior discoloration strongly matches Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.
